body.statement: In the experiment supplying \(e\), the bounded pseudo-outcome \(W=\frac{(A-e(X))Y}{e(X)[1-e(X)]}\) satisfies \(\mathbb E_P[W\mid X]=\tau(X)\). Consequently the constant-CATE problem reduces to classical nonadaptive \(L^2\) goodness-of-fit testing of a \(\gamma\)-Hölder regression function, and there exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) and \(n_0\), depending only on \(\gamma,d,L\), such that \(c r_{\mathrm{or}}(n)\le\rho_{n,e}^*\le C r_{\mathrm{or}}(n)\) for every \(n\ge n_0\).
body.justification: This standard benchmark isolates the classical signal-detection floor against which the observational nuisance penalty is measured.
body.gap: Spokoiny1996, Section 1, records the classical one-dimensional nonadaptive Hölder \(L^2\) boundary and develops its adaptive wavelet counterpart; the pseudo-outcome identity transports the standard \(d\)-dimensional analogue to the known-propensity causal experiment and is not a novelty claim.
body.consumer: The lemma fixes the comparator experiment needed to state the unknown-versus-known propensity frontier on one unchanged causal class.
